title: webSocket: a late error event of an old socket closes the new connection (unsubscribe and subscribe while CONNECTING, timeout with retry)
note: onerror has no check of the current socket. PR #6708 added that check to onclose only. Confidence high.

title: webSocket: an exception of the serializer becomes the error 'WebSocketSubject.error must be called with an object with an error code'
note: With a code property on the error, close() throws and the subject is stuck. Confidence high.

title: webSocket: error({code, reason}) with a reason over 123 bytes or a code that close() refuses leaves the socket open and the subject stuck
note: close() throws, so _resetState is skipped and no subscriber gets an event. Confidence high.

title: webSocket multiplex: a throwing subMsg still subscribes and sends unsubMsg, and an error of unsubMsg is lost
note: No return after observer.error in the subMsg catch. Confidence high.

title: webSocket: closingObserver is not called for a close that unsubscription causes, the one case that its documentation names
note: Only complete() and error() call it. Confidence high.

title: webSocket: the deprecated resultSelector option is typed and documented, but nothing reads it
note: Unused since 6.x. Confidence high.

title: webSocket: an explicit undefined deserializer or serializer replaces the JSON default
note: The config copy keeps own keys with the value undefined. Confidence medium.

title: webSocket: an exception in openObserver or closeObserver leaves the subject stuck
note: The hooks run unwrapped in the event handlers. Confidence medium: the contract for hook errors is not documented.

title: webSocket: values buffered before a connection are dropped when the attempt fails, so retry() does not send them
note: The docs say that the values are sent when the connection is established. The 8.x rewrite also drops them, so the docs may be the fault. Confidence low.

title: webSocket multiplex: after a connection loss, the unsubMsg of a stream goes out on the new connection
note: Some protocols, for example STOMP, answer an unknown UNSUBSCRIBE with an error. Confidence medium.

title: webSocket: values buffered before open stay in memory for the life of the connection
note: The queue subscription is not unsubscribed after the replay. Confidence medium.

title: webSocket: with no global WebSocket and no WebSocketCtor, the constructor throws ReferenceError, not the error of the library
note: The check uses the bare name WebSocket. Confidence high.

title: presence: the key __proto__ replaces the prototype of presenceState() and hides that member
note: transformState builds a plain object with assignment. Only the returned object changes, not Object.prototype. Confidence high.

title: connect() adds the connection handlers again at each connect, also at each automatic reconnect
note: After 20 reconnects, one frame runs 21 message callbacks. Confidence high.

title: disconnect() resolves but keeps a timer of 10 seconds, so a Node process cannot exit for 10 seconds
note: The id of the timeout timer is not kept or cleared. Confidence high.

title: connect() or subscribe() while the socket closes does nothing, and the channel stays in CHANNEL_ERROR
note: The guard isDisconnecting() drops the request. Confidence high.

title: the first phx_join has no access token, and the token is not pushed after the join
note: A regression of #2136 from the phoenix migration. Confidence high.

title: when the push buffer overflows, the promise of the dropped push does not settle
note: Only cancelTimeout() runs on the dropped push. Confidence high.

title: httpSend keeps its timeout timer when the fetch rejects
note: clearTimeout runs only after a resolved fetch. Confidence high.

title: each push failure on a joined channel is reported as 'before joining', and the real error is lost
note: A catch-all throws a fixed message with no cause. Confidence high.

title: a Uint8Array or Buffer broadcast payload goes out as JSON over the socket, but as binary over HTTP
note: The docs name only ArrayBuffer. Confidence low.

title: a binary frame of an unknown kind throws a TypeError in onmessage
note: The server sends only kind 4 today. Confidence low.

title: the type HeartbeatStatus has 'disconnected', but the callbacks of the user do not get it
note: The filter is intentional (#2496). Only the type is stale. Confidence low.

title: the maxPayload check of a batch counts base64 as 1.33 bytes for each byte, so the server answers 413 and the client closes
note: Base64 gives 4*ceil(n/3) bytes. Confidence high. The run suite-engineio-43922263433 of wirelab-suite-engineio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test max-payload-binary.

title: the Fetch transport sends credentials 'omit', so it drops same-origin cookies and breaks sticky sessions
note: XHR sends same-origin cookies. Shown in headless Chrome. Confidence high.

title: Fetch transport: an error while it reads the body is an unhandled rejection, so polling stops with no error event
note: res.text() has no catch. In Node.js the process exits. Confidence high.

title: WebTransport: the promises ready, createBidirectionalStream, pipeTo and write reject unhandled
note: Confidence high for ready, medium for pipeTo.

title: the heartbeat timer overflows when pingInterval + pingTimeout is over 2^31-1, so the client closes with 'ping timeout' at once
note: The server accepts that configuration. Confidence high. The run suite-engineio-43922263433 of wirelab-suite-engineio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test long-ping-interval.

title: a malformed open packet throws out of the transport callback, with no error or close event, and the socket stays 'opening'
note: JSON.parse and the field reads are unchecked. Only a server that does not obey the protocol causes it. Confidence high.

title: requestTimeout has no effect with NodeXHR, the default polling transport in Node.js, or with Fetch
note: xmlhttprequest-ssl has no timeout, and Fetch gets no AbortSignal. Browser XHR obeys it. Confidence medium. The run suite-engineio-43922263433 of wirelab-suite-engineio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test request-timeout.

title: close does not abort the polling requests in flight: the long-poll GET and the close POST
note: Each held request keeps a connection slot of the origin. Confidence medium. The run suite-engineio-43922263433 of wirelab-suite-engineio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test close-aborts-poll.

title: a failed probe is not closed: the probe WebSocket stays open, its listeners stay, and upgradeError fires twice
note: The else branch of _probe has no freezeTransport(). Confidence medium.

title: the types refuse perMessageDeflate: false and send(msg, fn), which the documentation and the runtime accept
note: The JSDoc default of perMessageDeflate is also wrong. Confidence high.

title: close during the polling handshake leaves a session on the server until 'ping timeout'
note: Reported before as #5274 (bug 2).

title: a close packet over WebSocket is ignored
note: Reported before as #5286.

title: close() in an 'upgrade' listener does not close the socket
note: Reported before as #5595.

title: In browsers, addEventListener listeners get close and error events with wrong fields: code "close", reason an Event object
note: cloneEventBrowser calls new e.constructor(e.type, e), but the own CloseEvent and ErrorEvent take other arguments. The upstream tests run only in Node and jsdom. Confidence high.

title: close(code, reason) with a code or reason that the WebSocket rejects leaves the inner socket open, and the error is lost
note: Since 1.2.0, _disconnect swallows the exception. readyState says CLOSED, send() still sends, and no close event comes. Confidence high.

title: reconnect() on an open socket stops itself when shouldReconnectOnClose returns false for its own close event
note: New in 1.3.0. The predicate is for automatic reconnects only. Different from the open issue #428. Confidence high.

title: A URL or query provider that rejects with undefined or null gives an unhandled rejection, no error event and no retry
note: Error(err.message) throws a TypeError inside the catch. The socket stays in CONNECTING. Confidence high.

title: updateProperties() throws "path must not start with a slash" on each PartySocket that was made with path
note: The constructor adds a slash to this.path, and updateProperties passes it back. Confidence high.

title: A second updateProperties() call undoes the first, and the id changes on each call
note: The merge uses the options of the constructor, which never change. A call with no id makes a new _pk. Confidence high for the undo, medium for the id.

title: React usePartySocket: after a mount with enabled false and a later enable, the first change of the options is ignored
note: The branch from false to true does not set socketInitializedRef. Related to the open issue #422, with a different cause. Confidence high.

title: Node and React Native: listeners get the reason "unknown reason" for an empty reason, and wasClean is always true
note: cloneEvent puts defaults on code and reason, and the own CloseEvent sets wasClean to true. Confidence high.

title: close() before the inner socket exists dispatches no close event
note: This occurs in the first tick, while a URL provider is pending, and during a backoff wait. The doc comment promises a terminal event. Confidence medium.

title: An on* handler that throws stops the addEventListener listeners, and an onclose that throws inside close() is lost
note: Inherited from reconnecting-websocket. The DOM reports the exception and runs the other listeners. Confidence medium.

title: The default reconnect delay has no jitter (3000 ms for each client), and the README tells a random default
note: PR #397 replaced the random value with a fixed midpoint and did not change the README. After a server restart, all clients connect at the same times. Confidence high.

title: reconnect() during a backoff wait does not connect until the old delay ends
note: _connectLock is held during _wait. Inherited from reconnecting-websocket. Confidence medium.

title: close() does not clear the backoff timer, so a Node process stays alive until the delay ends
note: The handle of the timer is not kept, so _clearTimeouts cannot clear it. Severity low. Confidence high.

title: room and party are not URL-encoded: a room with ? or # goes to the wrong room, or retries without end
note: Only a slash gives a warning. The server side must decode too. Confidence medium.

title: With no global crypto, new PartySocket() with no id throws ReferenceError
note: crypto?.randomUUID does not protect against a name that is not declared, so the fallback never runs. This occurs on React Native without a polyfill. Confidence high.

title: The types of partysocket/ws need the DOM lib
note: The declarations use AddEventListenerOptions, EventListenerOrEventListenerObject and BinaryType. The fault shows with skipLibCheck false. Confidence high.

title: The onError of the React hooks has the type Event, so e.message does not compile
note: use-handlers.ts uses the global WebSocketEventMap, not the own map of partysocket. Confidence high.

title: PartySocket.fetch needs room in its type also when basePath is given
note: getPartyInfo uses basePath in place of room, and the constructor accepts the same options with no room. Confidence medium.

title: A volatile event emitted while the namespace is not connected is buffered and sent after connect, not dropped
note: The check of the discard looks only at the transport. During the namespace handshake the transport is writable. Confidence high. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test volatile-before-connect.

title: A dropped volatile packet keeps its ack handler: the handler leaks, and emitWithAck never settles
note: _registerAckCallback runs before the discard, and the discard never removes the handler. Confidence high.

title: socket.connect() during a pending namespace handshake sends a second CONNECT
note: With WebSocket the server gets an orphan socket. With polling the server closes the whole connection, so each namespace drops. Confidence high. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test second-connect.

title: disconnect() during the namespace handshake leaves an orphan socket on the server
note: No DISCONNECT goes out, and the later CONNECT reply is ignored. A DISCONNECT sent at once makes the 4.8 server close the connection. Confidence high. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test disconnect-during-connect.

title: reconnectionAttempts 0, reconnectionDelay 0 and reconnectionDelayMax 0 in the constructor become the defaults
note: The constructor and backo2 use ||. The setters accept 0. randomizationFactor was fixed with ?? in #1231. Confidence high. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test reconnection-attempts-zero.

title: socket.recovered is undefined, not false, when the server does not use connection state recovery
note: The field has the type boolean. Low impact. Confidence high. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test recovered-false.

title: url() with no scheme in Node.js or React Native gives "undefined//host"
note: loc becomes false, so the check of typeof is always true and the https fallback never runs. Low impact. Confidence high.

title: socket.timeout(ms).emitWithAck() returns Promise<any>, and the type tests of the package do not run
note: FirstArg does not match the callback with two arguments. test:types is "exit 0", so the type test of the repository for this case never runs. Confidence high.

title: After about 1,015 reconnect attempts the backoff delay overflows to Infinity, and with jitter it drops near 0
note: Known upstream. The repro of this review shows 6 of 10 gaps under 200 ms after attempt 1031.

title: retries without ackTimeout: a positive ack goes to the callback as the error, and the event is sent three times
note: Known upstream. Related, different: issue #5446. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test retries-without-ack-timeout.

title: The retries queue keeps this.flags, so a later emit gets the timeout of an earlier one
note: Known upstream. The retries branch returns before this.flags = {}.

title: Connection state recovery: a volatile event with a string as its last argument becomes the offset, so recovery fails
note: Known upstream. PR #5547 closed with no merge on 2026-11-13. The commit f97d51a on main adds a check args.length > 1, thus an event with only its name no longer becomes the offset. A string as the last of two or more arguments still does. No release has f97d51a.

title: The decoder of the client allows 10 attachments, but the server sends more: an event with 11 buffers gives a parse error and a reconnect
note: Known upstream. The Manager makes the Decoder with no options. The run suite-socketio-43945837241 of wirelab-suite-socketio confirms it over NodeXHR and Fetch, with the it.fails test eleven-attachments.

title: close() in the tick of the constructor does not stop the /info request or its 8 s timer
note: InfoReceiver does not keep the handle of its setTimeout, and close() does not clear it. Related: issue #493 (closed by the stale bot). Confidence high.

title: After close(), the rest of the same a frame still gives message events, with readyState CLOSING
note: The a and m branches of the frame handler do not check readyState. WHATWG drops a message when the state is not OPEN. Confidence medium-high.

title: A malformed handshake leaves the client in the state unavailable for good, with no retry
note: The error branch of the handshake does not abort the runner or call retryIn, so connect() returns at once. The docs say that unavailable retries every 15 s. Confidence high.

title: Two test files bind port 50136, so a local run of the tests can fail with EADDRINUSE
note: integration.test.ts binds 50132 to 50136 and edge-cases.test.ts binds 50136, and the test files run in parallel. Both blocks skip when GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, so only a local run shows it. 6 of the 16 full runs of the fix tests (repro.yml, runs 43631168169 and 43631211204) failed with EADDRINUSE :::50136. Confidence high.

title: A pusher:error with a null code in the handshake throws a TypeError, and the client stays unavailable
note: getCloseAction gives null for a null code, and for each code below 4000 other than 1002 to 1004. The handshake passes the action null on, and ConnectionManager calls handshakeCallbacks[null]. The close path of the handshake changes null to backoff. Confidence high.

title: Channel names that are members of Object.prototype, such as constructor and __proto__, make subscribe() throw a TypeError
note: Channels keeps its table in a plain object and reads this.channels[name], so these names find the members of Object.prototype. The repro shows it for constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty and __proto__. Confidence high.

title: unsubscribe() of a pending subscription is lost after a reconnect, and the client subscribes again
note: subscribeAll() calls subscribe(), which clears subscriptionCancelled. Pull request 997 fixed it on master on 2026-10-29, after 8.6.0. Confidence high.

title: pusher.bind() callbacks get no argument when the event data is 0, false, null or an empty string
note: Dispatcher.emit adds the data only when it is truthy and no metadata comes with it. channel.bind() gets the value, because Channel gives metadata. Confidence high.

title: A presence channel_data that is not valid JSON gives an unhandled rejection, and the subscription stays pending
note: PresenceChannel.authorize calls JSON.parse in an async callback with no catch, so no pusher:subscription_error comes. By default, Node.js stops on an unhandled rejection. Confidence high.

title: A presence authorization with no channel_data and no signed-in user gives a subscription_error with the error undefined
note: PresenceChannel.authorize gives the string Invalid auth response to the callback, and Channel.subscribe reads error.message. Related: issue 485 (closed by the stale bot). Confidence high.

title: disconnect() after a close with a backoff code does not stop the reconnect
note: The backoff callback and the closed callback both call retryIn(1000), and retryIn replaces retryTimer but does not abort the old timer. disconnect() aborts only the second timer. switchCluster() in that second also gives a third connection. Confidence high.

title: connect() during the retry wait does not cancel the retry timer, which then closes the new connection
note: connect() starts a connection when there is no connection and no runner, but does not clear retryTimer. The timer calls disconnectInternally() and connect(), so the new connection closes with the code 1000 and a third one opens. Confidence high.

title: The configuration example of the README does not compile: channelAuthorization and userAuthentication require transport and endpoint
note: InternalAuthOptions makes transport and endpoint required, but the README gives defaults for both, and config.ts merges the defaults. Confidence high.

title: Channel.subscriptionCount has the type null, so a number does not compile
note: channel.ts declares subscriptionCount: null, and handleSubscriptionCountEvent sets the count. Confidence high.

title: The client sends more QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages in flight than the Receive Maximum of the server
note: [MQTT-3.3.4-7] [MQTT-4.9.0-2]. The tests flow_control2 and receive_maximum of suite-mqtt are it.fails.

title: The client sends packets larger than the Maximum Packet Size of the server
note: [MQTT-3.2.2-15]. A PUBLISH and a SUBSCRIBE go out above the limit. The tests maximum_packet_size of suite-mqtt are it.fails.

title: The client sends a PUBLISH with Topic Alias 0
note: [MQTT-3.3.2-8]. The test client_topic_alias of suite-mqtt is it.fails.

title: The client sends an unacknowledged PUBLISH again with DUP 0
note: [MQTT-3.3.1-1]. The resend after a reconnect has DUP 0, for MQTT 5.0 at QoS 1 and QoS 2 and for MQTT 3.1.1. The tests resend_with_dup_v5 and resend_with_dup_v311 are it.fails.

title: The client sends old messages again after Session Present 0, or on a new session with Clean Start 1
note: [MQTT-3.2.2-5] [MQTT-3.1.2-4] [MQTT-4.4.0-1]. The test resend_only_with_session of suite-mqtt is it.fails.

title: The client gives a new PUBLISH a Packet Identifier that is in use
note: [MQTT-2.2.1-3]. The test unique_packet_identifiers of suite-mqtt is it.fails.

title: The client sends a QoS 0 PUBLISH with DUP 1 when the application asks for it
note: [MQTT-3.3.1-2]. The client copies the dup option of the application into a QoS 0 PUBLISH. The test values_from_the_application is it.fails.

title: The client sends a Subscription Identifier in a PUBLISH when the application gives one
note: [MQTT-3.3.4-6]. The test values_from_the_application of suite-mqtt is it.fails.

title: A QoS 1 or QoS 2 publish that the client refuses for its Topic Alias does not settle
note: publish() gives _sendPacket no callback for QoS 1 and 2. The errors of _applyTopicAlias and _removeTopicAliasAndRecoverTopicName go to a no-op, and the Packet Identifier stays in outgoing. QoS 0 rejects. The tests topic_alias_maximum and client_topic_alias are it.fails.

title: A message listener that throws stops the other listeners and the rest of the frame, and xhr-polling stops with readyState OPEN
note: dispatchEvent of EventTarget starts each listener with no try/catch. Thus the exception goes up into the transport, and the rest of the a frame is lost. The xhr receiver moves bufferPosition after the emit, so its finish handler gives the same message again and throws before it emits close. Thus no next poll comes, and no close event. WHATWG DOM reports the exception and starts the next listener. Related: issue #563 (the repeated message, closed by the stale bot) and pull request #564 (open since 2021-09-08), which change only the receivers. Confidence high.

title: close(0) and close(NaN) do not throw InvalidAccessError, and close the socket with the code 1000
note: close() examines the code only when it is truthy (if (code && !userSetCode(code))), and then uses code || 1000. WHATWG throws InvalidAccessError for each code that is not 1000 or in 3000 to 4999, and [Clamp] unsigned short changes NaN to 0. The native WebSocket of Node.js throws for both. No upstream issue or pull request has it. Confidence high.

title: On a page loaded over https, new SockJS() throws SecurityError for http://localhost and http://*.localhost
note: The check of an insecure URL lets only 127.0.0.0/8 and [::1] through (isLoopbackAddr). Secure Contexts counts localhost and *.localhost as potentially trustworthy, so Mixed Content does not block them. Duplicate: issue #645 (open since 2024-01-11). Related: issue #482, where the maintainer declined localhost in 2019. Commit a57c910 then added 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 in 2020. Confidence medium-high.

title: close() while CONNECTING gives close 1000 with wasClean true, and an error event only while /info is pending
note: close() always gives _close() the code 1000 and wasClean true. The error event comes only when this._ir is set, so the events depend on an internal phase. WHATWG fails the connection: an error event, then close with the code 1006 and wasClean false, as the native WebSocket of Node.js does. This is not F0068, the timer of the /info request that close() leaks (issue #711). No upstream issue has it. Confidence medium-high.

title: close() while xhr-streaming waits for the page load does not stop it: on load, the closed socket connects and throws InvalidStateError
note: For a transport with needBody (xhr-streaming in a browser, jsonp-polling, the iframe transports), _connect() waits with attachEvent('load', this._connect.bind(this)). close() does not detach the listener or empty _transports. On load, _connect() opens a transport, and its open frame starts _open() on the closed socket. Then _close() throws InvalidStateError: SockJS has already been closed, from the transport callback. Related: issue #344 (the same error after an early close(), closed in 2017). Confidence high.

title: The timer of a transport that failed still runs, and it stops the next transport before the end of its own timeout
note: _connect() starts a new _transportTimeoutId for each transport, and _transportClose() does not clear the timer of the transport that failed. When the websocket transport fails fast, its timer stops the xhr-polling transport, and the socket closes with 2000 All transports failed. Pull request #607 fixed it on main on 2022-11-09, after 1.6.1 (2022-05-28), and no release has it. With the source of main, the review run 43396482043 opened with xhr-polling. Confidence high.

title: In Node.js, a connection that drops during an xhr-streaming response gives no close event, and readyState stays OPEN
note: The Node.js XHR driver listens only for the data and end events of the response and the error event of the request. When the connection drops after the response starts, the response gives no end, and the request gives no error, so finish does not come. The websocket and xhr-polling transports give close 1006. Related: issues #176 and #64 (a lost connection with no close event in browsers, closed in 2014) and pull request #601 (a heartbeat watchdog, open). Confidence high.

title: close() while a transport connects does not clear the transport timer, so Node.js stays alive to the end of the timeout
note: _connect() starts _transportTimeoutId, and only _open() clears it. _close() does not. SenderReceiver.close() removes its listeners first, so nothing starts _transportClose(), and the fix of pull request #607 on main does not cover this path. This is a different timer from that of F0068 (the /info request, issue #711, pull request #713). Confidence high.

title: A query that contains a second ? loses its end on each request
note: addPath() of lib/utils/url.js splits the URL at each "?" and keeps only the first two parts. So the query ?next=/home?tab=2&token=abc becomes ?next=/home on the /info request and on each request of the transport. RFC 3986 (section 3.4) permits "?" in a query, and the README of sockjs-client permits a query in the URL. Issues #72 and #248 (closed) are about other losses of the query. Confidence high.

title: Two adjacent stream arguments: the client sends the second one as a plain argument, with no stream id
note: The function _replaceStreamingParams() of HubConnection removes each stream argument with args.splice(), but it does not decrease the index. So the loop does not examine the next argument. A call of invoke() with two adjacent Subject arguments sends one stream id. The second Subject goes into the arguments as {"observers":[]}. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: A callback of onclose, onreconnecting or onreconnected that throws stops the callbacks after it
note: HubConnection puts one try/catch block around the forEach() loop of each list of these callbacks. When a callback throws, the client logs the error and skips the callbacks after it. Thus a library that registers its callback after the app does not get the event. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: After a failed stateful reconnect, the automatic reconnect connects, but the client sends no message and gets no message
note: Only _completeClose() disposes the MessageBuffer, and _startInternal() makes a new buffer only for a stateful connection. So the old buffer stays in its reconnect mode. It keeps each send and drops each received message until a Sequence message comes, and a server with no stateful reconnect sends none. The onreconnected event comes, and the pings keep the connection open. In the repro, invoke() is still pending after 1000 ms. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: With stateful reconnect, the client does not count a message that comes in the frame of the handshake response
note: HubConnection makes the MessageBuffer only after the handshake promise resolves, and a message in the frame of the handshake response comes before that. On the first start, the app gets the message, but the buffer does not count it. So the sequence ids of the client are 1 less than those of the server. After a stateful reconnect, the app gets a message 2 times. After an automatic reconnect, the old buffer drops the message. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: With Server-Sent Events, a connect that fails does not close its EventSource, and the EventSource continues to reconnect
note: In ServerSentEventsTransport.connect(), the onerror handler before the open rejects the promise, but it does not close the EventSource. The transport keeps the EventSource in _eventSource only after the open, so stop() cannot close it. In the repro, start() rejects after 1 GET request, and 3.5 s later the client has sent 4 GET requests. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: The client continues to send an upload stream after the server completed the invocation
note: HubProtocol.md tells the caller to stop its StreamItem and Completion messages after the Completion of the callee. The function _launchStreams() of HubConnection subscribes to each upload stream and does not dispose the subscription. In the repro, the client sends 4 messages for upload stream 0 after the Completion of the server. The same occurs after stream().dispose(). No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: Two promises of the client reject with a string, not with an Error
note: WebSocketTransport.send() gives Promise.reject("WebSocket is not in the OPEN state"), and TransportSendQueue rejects with "Connection stopped.". So send() and invoke() reject with a string when the socket closes, or when the connection stops with sends in the queue. A caller that reads error.message gets undefined, and the rejection has no stack. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: With a binary hub protocol, the client decodes the handshake response as Latin-1, not as UTF-8
note: HandshakeProtocol.parseHandshakeResponse() changes the bytes into text with String.fromCharCode.apply(), one character for each byte. HubProtocol.md specifies UTF-8 JSON for the handshake. So the client garbles each character of an error text that is not ASCII: "unterstützt" becomes "unterstÃ¼tzt". The text path decodes correctly. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: A client method with the name of a member of Object.prototype, for example "constructor", breaks on() and the client results
note: HubConnection keeps its handlers in this._methods, a plain object, so this._methods["constructor"] is the function Object. on("constructor", fn) throws the TypeError "this._methods[methodName].indexOf is not a function". A client-result call of the server for "constructor" gets no Completion, so the server waits for its own timeout. A Map or Object.create(null) prevents it. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: @microsoft/signalr loads tough-cookie at run time, but it does not declare it as a dependency
note: FetchHttpClient calls requireFunc("tough-cookie") on Node.js. The package.json of @microsoft/signalr has tough-cookie only in its overrides, which have no effect on a consumer. An npm install works because npm hoists the tough-cookie of fetch-cookie. In a strict layout (pnpm with no hoist, Yarn Plug'n'Play), build() throws "Cannot find module 'tough-cookie'". Issue #52656 (a CookieJar fault in Electron, open) has possibly the same cause. Issue #51849 (closed) is about the version of tough-cookie only. Confidence high.

title: After stop() and start(), the Ack timer of the old connection sends its sequence id on the new connection
note: MessageBuffer._dispose() does not clear _ackTimerHandle, and the timer sends through the HttpConnection object that the next connection also uses. In the repro, the app stops and starts in 1 second, and the client sends Ack 3 on a new connection that has received no message. A server that trusts this Ack removes messages from its resend buffer that the client did not get. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: The check for multiple client results does not count a falsy result, so the outcome depends on the order of the handlers
note: The function _invokeClientMethod() of HubConnection sends the error "Client provided multiple results." only if expectsResponse && res && prevRes is true. So 5 and 7 give the error, and 0 and 7 give the result 7. Also, 7 and 0 give 0, and true and false give false. Pull request #45169 (merged) changed the Completion of a false or null result, but not this check. Confidence high.

title: The typings tell that the client sets IStreamSubscriber.closed when the stream closes, but nothing sets it
note: Stream.ts declares closed?: boolean with the comment "A boolean that will be set by the IStreamResult when the stream is closed." No code of the client sets it. After a completion, an error or dispose(), subscriber.closed stays undefined. No upstream issue tells this fault. Confidence high.

title: The timeout and the abort signal of FetchHttpClient stop when the response headers come, so a stalled body blocks stop()
note: The finally block of FetchHttpClient.send() clears the timeout and request.abortSignal.onabort when fetch() resolves, before deserializeContent() reads the body. So a long poll whose body stalls after its headers does not time out, and LongPollingTransport.stop() cannot abort it. In the repro, stop() is still pending after 2000 ms, in the state Disconnecting. Issue #58260 (open) has possibly the same cause. Confidence high.

title: An inbound QoS 2 PUBLISH with a Topic Alias and an empty topic arrives with the topic ""
note: [MQTT-3.3.2-12]. handlePublish puts the topic of the alias in a local variable, but for QoS 2 it stores the packet, and the PUBREL handler emits 'message' with the topic of the stored packet, which is still empty. QoS 0 and QoS 1 use the topic of the alias. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: A SUBACK with one failure code removes each topic of its SUBSCRIBE from the resubscribe list
note: handleAck deletes each topic of messageIdToTopic[messageId] from _resubscribeTopics when one reason code is a failure. So a topic that the server granted is not subscribed again after a reconnect with a new session. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: With the option servers and TLS, the SNI and the certificate check keep the name of the first server
note: connect/tls.ts sets opts.servername to the first host. The failover wrapper of connect/index.ts changes opts.host and opts.hostname, but not opts.servername. So the ClientHello to the second server has the SNI of the first server, and tls.connect checks its certificate against the first name. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: publish() with QoS 1 or 2 after end() throws a TypeError when reconnectPeriod is 0
note: After end(), publish() with QoS 1 throws "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'set')", and publishAsync() rejects with the same TypeError. The callback of publish() does not get an error that tells that the client is closed. Confidence high.

title: The client sends a QoS 2 PUBLISH to a server whose CONNACK gives Maximum QoS 1
note: [MQTT-3.2.2-11]. No file of MQTT.js reads the maximumQoS property of the CONNACK, and the callback of publish() gets no error. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: The client sends a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 to a server whose CONNACK gives Retain Available 0
note: [MQTT-3.2.2-14]. No file of MQTT.js reads the retainAvailable property of the CONNACK, and the callback of publish() gets no error. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: An offline subscribe() gets "Connection closed" when a reconnect attempt fails, but the client still sends the SUBSCRIBE
note: _flushVolatile calls the callback with "Connection closed" and deletes the outgoing entry, but it keeps the queued SUBSCRIBE and the topic in _resubscribeTopics. So the next connection subscribes, and the app thinks that it has no subscription. In the repro, the server also gets the SUBSCRIBE twice on that connection. Confidence high.

title: unsubscribe() reports success for an UNSUBACK with a failure reason code
note: MQTT 5.0 section 3.11.3: a reason code of 0x80 or more is a failure. handleAck calls the callback of unsubscribe() with no error for each UNSUBACK, and unsubscribeAsync() resolves. For a SUBACK with a failure code, subscribe() gives an error. The same code is on main (0ceae41). Confidence high.

title: end() before connect() of a client with manualConnect throws a TypeError
note: With manualConnect: true, the client has no stream until connect(). end() then throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on')". Confidence high.

title: Five test files call process.exit(0) in an after hook, so node --test does not report a failure of the last test of each file and exits 0
note: client.ts, client_mqtt5.ts, secure_client.ts, unique_message_id_provider_client.ts and websocket_client.ts in test/node, at 5.16.1 (66a9708) and at main 0ceae41. The script unit-test:node runs the files with node --test. With the hook, the runner does not report the last test of the file, and a failure of that test gives exit code 0. A comment of client_mqtt5.ts names the effect, and the tests of GHSA-h8jm-hm87-fqw3 are not last because of it. Found in the work on the fix of F0116 (MQTT.js #2108), whose new test is not last for the same reason. On Windows with Node 24.21.0 the repro printed BUG PRESENT and exited 1. Confidence high.

title: A lone UTF-16 surrogate in a string is written as invalid UTF-8, so protobufjs cannot decode its own proto3 message
note: util.utf8.write writes ED A0 80 for a lone surrogate. TextEncoder and Buffer write EF BF BD. The decoder of protobufjs rejects these bytes in a proto3 or editions string field (utf8_validation VERIFY). On Node.js, a string of 40 chars or more goes through Buffer and is correct. Confidence high.

title: The .proto parser drops the Unicode escapes of a string literal
note: protoc and the language specification read a backslash, u and 4 hex digits (or U and 8 hex digits) as a code point. The unescape function of tokenize.js removes the escape and keeps the digits as text. Confidence high.

title: An octal or hex escape of a byte above 0x7f in a .proto string gives a char, not a byte
note: protoc reads each octal or hex escape as one byte. protobufjs makes one char of each escape. A string default with escaped UTF-8 bytes gets the wrong text, and a bytes default gets the UTF-8 form of each char: the escape of 0xff gives c3 bf, not ff. Confidence high.

title: A bytes default that looks like base64 is decoded as base64
note: Field#resolve decodes the string default of a bytes field as base64 when util.base64.test accepts it, and else writes its UTF-8 bytes. A .proto default is a string literal (protoc), so the default text test gives the bytes b5 eb 2d, not 74 65 73 74. Confidence high.

title: A 64-bit default larger than 2^53 in a .proto file loses its low bits
note: parseNumber of parse.js gives a float for each number. Field#resolve then makes a Long of the float, so 9007199254740993 becomes 9007199254740992. protoc keeps the exact value. Confidence high.

title: The .proto parser rejects a hex number with the prefix 0X
note: The protobuf language specification and protoc accept the prefixes 0x and 0X. The regular expressions of parse.js accept only 0x, so a field number or a default such as 0X1F throws an error. Confidence high.

title: For a Media Sequence Number of 2^32 or more, the AES-128 IV that hls.js derives keeps only the low 32 bits
note: RFC 8216, section 5.2, puts the full number in 16 octets. This rule applies when the EXT-X-KEY tag has no IV attribute. createInitializationVector of level-key.ts uses the 32-bit operator >>. Thus the first 16-byte block of each segment decrypts wrong. Confidence high.

title: An IV attribute with fewer than 32 hex digits gives an IV of fewer than 16 bytes, so the segment does not decrypt
note: RFC 8216 defines the IV as a 128-bit unsigned integer, and a hexadecimal-sequence has no minimum length. AttrList.hexadecimalInteger does not pad on the left, so IV=0x1 gives one byte, and WebCrypto rejects it. Confidence medium: a maintainer can read the RFC as a requirement of 32 digits.

title: The Variable Name constructor or toString gives a false duplicate error, and an undefined reference to it gives no parsing error
note: variable-substitution.ts keeps the variables in a plain object and tests a name with the operator in, so the names of Object.prototype match. The substitution then puts the text of a native function into the URI. The IMPORT attribute has the same fault. Confidence high.

title: An EXT-X-DATERANGE tag with the ID toString or constructor makes parseLevelPlaylist throw a TypeError
note: m3u8-parser.ts looks for an earlier Date Range with the same ID in a plain object. The lookup finds a function of Object.prototype, and the DateRange constructor reads its start date, which is undefined. Confidence high.

title: After a truncated multi-byte sequence at the end of the data, Utf8ErrorFuncs.replace and ignore drop the valid bytes that follow it
note: For the reason OVERRUN, ignoreFunc of utils/utf8.ts returns the count of all remaining bytes, so the decoder skips to the end. Thus the bytes E2 41 decode to one U+FFFD with replace, and TextDecoder gives U+FFFD and A.

title: A socket frame that is not JSON, or an eth_subscription message with no params, gives an unhandled rejection and no error event
note: SocketProvider._processMessage is async. It calls JSON.parse with no try, and it reads result.params.subscription with no check. Since 6.4.0 (ethers #4051), only a JSON message of unknown form gives the error event. In the default mode of Node.js, the unhandled rejection stops the process.

title: SocketSubscriber.stop does not remove the subscriber from the map of the provider, so each on() and off() keeps one subscriber in memory
note: SocketProvider._register puts each subscriber in the private map #subs, and no code removes it. In the repro, 50 cycles of on() and off() keep 50 subscribers after garbage collection. With a delete in stop(), the count is 0.

title: The encoder writes a lone UTF-16 surrogate as invalid UTF-8 in a string of 50 characters or fewer, but as U+FFFD in a longer string
note: utf8Encode uses utf8EncodeJs for 50 characters or fewer, and TextEncoder.encodeInto for a longer string. utf8EncodeJs writes U+D800 as ED A0 80, which is not valid UTF-8. TextEncoder writes EF BF BD. In the repro, 3 short strings give invalid UTF-8, and the same strings with 60 more characters give U+FFFD.

title: encode() writes an Invalid Date as the timestamp 0 with no error, so decode() gives the valid date 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
note: encodeDateToTimeSpec gives NaN for sec and nsec. encodeTimeSpecToTimestamp then uses the timestamp 96 format, and DataView writes NaN as 0. In the repro, new Date(NaN) and new Date("not a date") both decode as 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.

title: An event type that is the name of an Object.prototype member, for example toString, makes send() of an event stream reject with a TypeError
note: EventStreamSerde.deserializeEventStream in @smithy/core 3.41.0 tests unionMember in memberSchemas, and memberSchemas is a plain object. The same function uses hasOwn for the event keys. In the repro of SelectObjectContent, the unknown event type FutureEvent is skipped, but toString, constructor and __proto__ make send() reject with "eventStreamSchema.isStructSchema is not a function".

title: An event stream that ends after 1 to 3 bytes of the length of a new message ends with no error, but a later cut gives "Truncated event message received."
note: When the source ends, getChunkedStream in @smithy/core 3.41.0 examines only currentMessageTotalLength, so it drops a part of the 4-byte length prefix. In the repro of SelectObjectContent, cuts after 1, 2 and 3 bytes of the second message end with no error, and cuts after 4, 5 and 12 bytes throw.

title: The XML parser gives a wrong character for a numeric character reference above U+FFFF, for example 😀 gives U+F600
note: decodeEntities in @aws-sdk/xml-builder 3.972.43 uses String.fromCharCode, which keeps the low 16 bits. In the repro of ListObjectsV2, 😀 and 😀 give U+F600, and 𐀀 gives U+0000. String.fromCodePoint with a range check gives the correct character.

title:
The XML parser changes a value of only white space with a line feed from character references, for example 
, to an empty string
note:
The parser of @aws-sdk/xml-builder 3.972.43 applies the rule text.trim() === "" && text.includes("
") after it decodes the character references. In the repro of ListObjectsV2, the keys 
, 
 and " 
 " become "", and the keys a
 and 	 stay correct.

title: The XML parser changes an undeclared entity with no error:   becomes empty, and &constructor; becomes the source text of a function
note: decodeEntities in @aws-sdk/xml-builder 3.972.43 returns AwsXmlParser.ENTITIES[name] ?? "", and ENTITIES is a plain object. In the repro of ListObjectsV2, a b gives "ab", and a&constructor;b gives "afunction Object() { [native code] }b". parseTag has the same plain-object test, child.tag in obj: x gives [Function: toString, "x"], but no S3 shape reads such a member.

title: The stream reader reads a stream cut inside the 8-byte prefix of a message as a complete stream, with no error
note: RecordBatchStreamReader of apache-arrow 21.2.0 throws when a stream stops inside the metadata of a message. When it stops after 2, 4, 6 or 8 bytes of the prefix of the RecordBatch, tableFromIPC returns the schema with 0 rows and no error. The repro reads 4 cut streams of a valid stream of 3 rows.

title: The stream reader reads a RecordBatch whose dictionary was never sent, and the column gives null for each row, with no error
note: The format sends the DictionaryBatch of an id before each RecordBatch that uses it. In apache-arrow 21.2.0, a stream with no DictionaryBatch gives 3 rows, d = [null, null, null], from a column that was ["a", "b", "a"]. The repro removes the DictionaryBatch from a valid stream.

title: The writer writes a wrong second batch when two batches share the first chunk of a dictionary and then differ
note: In apache-arrow 21.2.0, the shared chunk ["a", "b"] concatenated with ["c"], then with ["X"], gives the written batches ["a", "b", "c"] and ["a", "X"]. The stream and the file read back ["a", "b", "c"] and ["a", "c"]. RecordBatchWriter._writeDictionaries() compares only the first chunk and the number of chunks with the previous dictionary, so it writes no DictionaryBatch for the second batch.

title: The file reader accepts two non-delta DictionaryBatches for one id, and the values of the column change with no error
note: The format lets a file have one non-delta DictionaryBatch for each id, and the writer of apache-arrow 21.2.0 refuses a replacement. The file reader accepts one: with the isDelta byte of the second DictionaryBatch set to 0, the column ["a", "b", "c"] reads as ["c", null, null].

title: The client sends 288 of the 1092 code units of escapable_by_client with no escape, for example U+2028 and U+FEFF
note: The section JSON Unicode Encoding of the protocol says that the browser must escape the characters of escapable_by_client. quote() of lib/utils/escape.js in 1.6.1 escapes only the output of JSON.stringify and its own list extraEscapable. A probe of the review and the check client-escapes of the SockJS suite give the raw units U+007F-U+009F, U+00AD, U+0600-U+0604, U+070F, U+17B4-U+17B5, U+2002-U+20CF, U+20D2-U+20D3, U+20D8-U+20E6, U+20EA-U+20FF and U+FEFF on each of the 4 transports.

title: The HTTP batch matches each reply to a request by its position after a sort, so a reply with the id null moves the other replies
note: JSON-RPC 2.0 gives the id null to a reply when the server cannot read the id of the request. viem 2.58.0 sorts the replies of a batch by id and matches them by position. In the repro, address 2 gets the error and address 3 gets the balance of address 2, with no error.

title: An IPC frame that is not valid JSON throws out of the socket data listener, an uncaught exception
note: utils/rpc/ipc.ts parses each frame with JSON.parse and no try/catch. The WebSocket path has one. In the repro, the frame {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"result":} gives an uncaught SyntaxError, and the request times out.

title: One stray closing brace from the IPC server drops each later reply on the socket
note: The frame splitter of utils/rpc/ipc.ts counts braces and lets the depth go below 0. After one } outside a message, the depth stays at -1 for the life of the socket. In the repro, three requests with valid replies time out.

title: The unsubscribe() function of a WebSocket subscription stays pending when the socket is closed
note: unsubscribe() sends eth_unsubscribe with no onError (clients/transports/webSocket.ts). utils/rpc/socket.ts gives the send error to the undefined onError, so the error is lost. In the repro, the promise is pending 5 s after the server drops the socket.

title: With reconnect: false, a WebSocket frame that is not JSON leaves the old socket open, and the next request opens a second socket
note: attemptReconnect() of utils/rpc/socket.ts clears the maps and removes the client from the cache, but it does not close the socket. In the repro, the server has 2 open sockets from one client.

title: decodeAbiParameters decodes data that ends before the head of a later static parameter from a wrong position, with no error
note: After a top-level dynamic parameter, the cursor stays at byte 32. In viem 2.58.0, 96 bytes for 4 heads (128 bytes) decode to [3n, 119n, "\u0000\u0000\u0000", 119n]. The expected result is a bounds error.

title: trim() of a hex value to the right removes zero nibbles, not zero bytes, and gives a shifted value
note: In viem 2.58.0, trim("0x1020", { dir: "right" }) gives 0x0102, and the byte path gives 0x1020. The hex path removes the last zero nibble, and the value of odd length gets a pad on the left.

title: The IPC subscribe() stays pending when the socket closes before the reply
note: clients/transports/ipc.ts sends eth_subscribe with no onError. The WebSocket transport gives one. In the repro, the server closes the socket at the subscribe request. The promise is pending after 5 s, and onError has 0 calls.

title: The rank of fallback() gives the score NaN when each sampled latency is 0 ms, so a failing transport stays first
note: The latency score is 1 - meanLatency / maxLatency, which is NaN when maxLatency is 0. The sort keeps the order for NaN. The repro freezes Date.now(), as for a fast local transport that answers in one 1 ms step.

title: An HTTP 200 reply with an empty body resolves the request with undefined, not with an error
note: utils/rpc/http.ts parses an empty body as {}, which has no result and no error. In the repro, sendRawTransaction resolves with undefined in place of a hash or an error.

title: A JS regex flag g is written as the BSON option s (dotAll), and the JS flag s is dropped
note: parser/serializer.ts writes global as 's' and drops dotAll, and the options are not in alphabetical order. parser/deserializer.ts reads 's' back as the JS flag g.

title: calculateObjectSize and serialize do not agree for typed arrays, DataView and ArrayBuffer
note: calculateObjectSize counts each ArrayBuffer view as binary. serialize writes a typed array other than Uint8Array, a DataView or an ArrayBuffer as a document. An ArrayBuffer comes back as {}.

title: fieldsAsRaw matches the names of Object.prototype, so an array named constructor comes back raw
note: parser/deserializer.ts reads fieldsAsRaw[name] through the prototype chain. With fieldsAsRaw { plain: false }, the arrays constructor and toString come back as raw bytes.

title: A bigint outside the int64 range is written modulo 2^64, with no error
note: serialize and EJSON.stringify write 2n**64n + 5n as 5, and 2n**63n as -2n**63n. The value that comes back is a different number. The upstream tests pin this wrap on purpose (test/node/bigint.test.ts: 'truncates a BigInt that is larger than a 64-bit int'), so it is the intended behavior and no PR goes out.

title: An Invalid Date is written as the datetime 0, and a datetime outside the Date range comes back as 0
note: serialize writes new Date(NaN) as 1970-01-01 with no error. A valid datetime of 2^62 ms is read as an Invalid Date, so a round trip writes 0.

title: A cut int64 value with useBigInt64 throws RangeError, not BSONError
note: With useBigInt64 true, a document with only 3 bytes of an int64 value throws RangeError from BigInt(NaN). The default path throws BSONError.

title: EJSON $binary accepts a bad subType as 0 and bad base64 as empty data
note: EJSON.parse turns the subType "100" and "zz" into 0. On Node.js, the base64 "!!!!" becomes empty data.

title: EJSON number wrappers accept out-of-range and non-numeric strings and change the value
note: $numberInt "2147483648" becomes -2147483648 and "12abc" becomes 0. $numberLong 2^63 becomes -2^63, and a $timestamp t of 2^32 becomes 0 in canonical mode.

title: A 404 reply with an empty body, as each 404 reply to HEAD, becomes success with status 204 and no error
note: processResponse turns a 404 with an empty body into 204 No Content, as a workaround for postgrest-js#295. A reply to HEAD has no body, so a count with head: true on a missing table gives count null and no error.

title: A failed reply whose body is a JSON scalar (null, false, 0 or "") gives no error object
note: processResponse uses JSON.parse(body) as the error and does not check that it is an object. A 500 with the body null gives success true and error null. false, 0 and "" give a falsy error, so if (error) and throwOnError() do not see the failure.

title: Retry-After in the HTTP-date form is read as 0 seconds, so the retry of a 503 starts at once
note: fetchWithRetry uses parseInt(retryAfter, 10) || 0. RFC 9110 10.2.3 also allows an HTTP-date, which parseInt reads as NaN. The delay also has no upper limit.

title: The timeout option stops when the headers arrive, so a response body that stalls hangs the query with no limit
note: withTimeout clears its timer when fetch resolves, and processResponse then reads the body with res.text() with no guard. The doc of the option says that it prevents indefinite hangs.

title: rpc() with get: true sends an object argument as the text [object Object]
note: rpc() uses POST for object arguments only when head is true. With get: true, each argument goes into the URL as a template string, so a json argument becomes [object Object].

title: eq(), neq() and match() accept array and JSON column values by type, but send them as a,b and [object Object]
note: The value type is the column type, so string[] type-checks for a text[] column and an object for a jsonb column. At run time the value goes into the URL as a template string, which Postgres rejects or reads as a different value.

title: rpc() with count replaces the Prefer header of the client, so a client with tx=rollback commits that call
note: rpc() uses headers.set('Prefer', ...) for count, and each table method uses headers.append. So each Prefer preference of the client headers, for example tx=rollback or timezone, is lost only for rpc() with count.

title: The error of a failed query result is a plain object, not the declared PostgrestError: instanceof is false and toJSON() is missing
note: The declared type of PostgrestResponseFailure.error is the class PostgrestError. processResponse returns the parsed body or { message }. Only throwOnError() and getOpenApiSpec() make instances.

title: With excludeOperationName and method GET, a mutation is sent with GET
note: analyzeDocument gives isMutation false when excludeOperationName is set, before it parses the document. So the client uses its own method for a mutation, and the variables go into the URL. Without the option, the client sends a mutation with POST. A server that obeys GraphQL over HTTP refuses a mutation over GET.

title: batchRequests() with method GET throws a TypeError when the batch has a mutation
note: batchRequests keeps method in the fetch options. The fetch init spreads them after the computed POST, so the request is a GET with a body, and fetch rejects it before it sends. request() and rawRequest() take method out of the fetch options.

title: A batch reply with a GraphQL error gives a ClientError with no errors and the message GraphQL Error (Code: 200)
note: The response of the error spreads the array of results into an object, so its keys are 0, 1 and so on. response.errors is undefined, and the message does not name the GraphQL error.

title: With method GET, the query cleaner changes string literals: a # cuts the rest of the line, and commas and runs of spaces change
note: cleanQuery is one regular expression that does not skip strings. A string such as "C# tips" ends the query at the #, so the server gets a query that does not parse. Issue #378 (2024) reported the comma part.

title: setHeader() has no effect when the client headers are a Headers instance, an array or a function
note: setHeader does headers[key] = value. On a Headers instance, an array or a function, this sets a JavaScript property, and the requests do not get the header. The client accepts each of these types. Issue #298 (2024) reported the Headers case.

title: A request header does not replace a client header whose name differs only in case: the request sends the two values
note: The client merges the two header sets as plain objects, with keys that are case-sensitive. Authorization from the client and authorization from the request become the header "Bearer old, Bearer new". A Headers instance always gives lowercase names.

title: With a BigInt variable, a GraphQL error becomes a TypeError from the ClientError constructor
note: The constructor makes its message with JSON.stringify of the request, and the variables have the BigInt. The jsonSerializer option can send a BigInt, but the error path does not use it. The caller loses the GraphQL error, and instanceof ClientError is false.

title: rawRequest() with an options object gives the responseMiddleware variables: undefined
note: rawRequest passes the positional variables argument to the responseMiddleware, which is undefined when the call uses an options object. request() passes the variables of its options.

title: geopos() drops each member that has no position, so the next positions move to the wrong members
note: transform() in geo_pos.ts skips each null entry of the GEOPOS reply. Redis gives one entry for each member in order, with null for a member that is not in the key, so entry i of the result is not the position of member i.

title: keys() and scan() give key names that JSON parsing changed
note: The automatic deserialization runs JSON.parse on each key name: "123" comes back as the number 123, "null" as null and "\"draft\"" as "draft". The docs give string[]. del() with a changed name deletes a different key.

title: A function that throws a falsy value gives the caller a success
note: The reply and the caller test the truth of the thrown value. A function that throws undefined, null, 0, '' or false, or that gives Promise.reject() with no reason, resolves the call with undefined.

title: An onRequest hook that does not wait for next() leaves the call open after the timeout
note: The type of onRequest allows a void return. When the hook calls next() and returns, _call clears the timer and removes the pending call, so the reply is dropped and the timeout never rejects the call.

title: The Node.js URL storage finds the uploads of other fingerprints that start with the same text
note: FileUrlStorage searches with the prefix tus::<fingerprint> and no :: at the end. findPreviousUploads() for photo-1 gives the uploads of photo-12, and a resume of one continues the upload of the other file. The browser storage is correct. Also on main (5.0.0-pre3).

title: A metadata key with a space or a comma changes the pairs that the server reads
note: encodeMetadata() writes each key as it is. The protocol forbids an empty key and keys with spaces or commas. The key project name is lost, and owner,team gives the keys owner and team. Also on main (5.0.0-pre3).

title: abort() before the first request does not stop the upload
note: start() waits for the fingerprint and the file, then _startSingleUpload() sets _aborted to false again. The upload sends its requests and calls onSuccess after abort(). The open pull request tus-js-client #929 of a maintainer changes this. Also on main (5.0.0-pre3).

title: A URL storage that cannot save the upload stops the upload with no callback
note: _createUpload() calls _saveUploadInUrlStorage().then() with no catch. When addUpload() rejects, no PATCH request goes out, neither onSuccess nor onError runs, and the rejection is not handled. Main (5.0.0-pre3) gives onError.

title: A resumed parallel upload writes the part URLs into the boundaries of the app
note: _startParallelUpload() sets part.uploadUrl on the objects of parallelUploadBoundaries. A later upload of another file with the same array resumes the old parts, sends none of its bytes and reports success. Main (5.0.0-pre3) copies the objects.

title: sign() of a GET or HEAD Request with a Content-Type header throws a TypeError
note: sign() reads the body of a Request input when it has a Content-Type header. For GET and HEAD that body is an empty ArrayBuffer, and new Request() refuses it. No request goes out.

title: sign() of a Request drops its signal and its redirect mode
note: sign() copies only the method, URL, headers and body of a Request input. An abort of the Request does not stop aws.fetch(), and redirect: manual becomes follow.

title: The guess gives a wrong service and region for a virtual-hosted bucket on an S3 host with a dash
note: my-bucket.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com gives the service my-bucket and the region s3-us-west-2. The guess knows the dash hosts only in the path style.

title: The guess gives the service s3-accesspoint for an S3 access point host
note: The signing name of S3 access points is s3. The credential scope is wrong, and the S3 rules (UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD) do not apply.

title: The stream reader drops a message of an unexpected type but not its body, and parses the body as the next messages
note: A parser differential: in the same bytes, a reader that frames by bodyLength sees one RecordBatch of 3 rows, and apache-arrow 21.2.0 reads 6 rows, [666, 777, 888, 1, 2, 3]. The project rated it a regular bug, not a security fault.

title: tableFromIPC loops with no end on a file whose RecordBatch block points at a DictionaryBatch
note: The file reader reads the block as a DictionaryBatch, does not advance, and reads the same block again. The call never returns. The project rated it a regular bug, not a security fault.

title: The IPC reader accepts buffer regions outside the message body, and rows read as undefined with no error
note: subarray() clamps a buffer that ends after the body, so no read goes outside the body. But rows read as undefined and toArray() is shorter than numRows, with no error. Arrow C++ refuses such a buffer. The project rated it a regular bug, not a security fault.

title: The IPC reader ignores Schema.endianness: a big-endian stream reads 1, 2, 3 as 16777216, 33554432, 50331648
note: The reader neither swaps the bytes nor refuses the stream. The project rated it a regular bug, not a security fault.

title: With structuredClone and useRecords: false, unpack() throws a TypeError for an object that refers to itself
note: The id extension makes a Map placeholder for a msgpack map, but with mapsAsObjects the map reads as a plain object, and the copy step calls targetProperties.entries(). An array that refers to itself works.

title: With moreTypes, an Error whose name is an Object.prototype member does not come back as an Error
note: unpack() calls errors[name](message) with no own-property check. The names constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty and isPrototypeOf give a String, a string, an object or a boolean, and __proto__ makes unpack() throw.

title: With useFloat32 DECIMAL_ROUND or DECIMAL_FIT, a float32 Infinity, -Infinity or NaN unpacks as 0
note: The rounding uses >> 0, which makes each non-finite value 0. roundFloat32() has the same fault. msgpackr packs these values as float64, but another encoder can send them as float32.

title: The server sends the result of a completed operation to a new operation with the same id, and drops the result of the new one
note: PROTOCOL.md lets a client re-use an id after it completes the operation. Each operation deletes ctx.subscriptions[id] in a finally block, so an old operation that ends late answers for the new one and deletes its reservation.

title: client.iterate(): throw() ends the iterator but does not dispose the subscription
note: return() sends complete and releases the connection. throw() only marks the iterator done, so the server keeps sending values, the client keeps them in a list, and the lazy socket stays open.

title: Presence.syncDiff changes the state that it is given and returns the same object
note: syncState copies its input state. syncDiff removes the left metas from the presence objects of its input, and for a null-prototype state (each state that syncState and syncDiff return) it changes and returns that object, so a caller that keeps the previous state sees it change.

title: After the fallback to LongPoll, the socket keeps the custom encode and decode, which a LongPoll socket ignores
note: The constructor uses opts.encode and opts.decode only when the transport is not LongPoll. replaceTransport changes only the transport, so a socket that falls back with longPollFallbackMs keeps the custom serializer over LongPoll.

title: The Accept field gives application/json the same weight as application/graphql-response+json
note: createClient sends accept: application/graphql-response+json, application/json (src/client.ts line 241), after the headers of the caller, so the caller cannot change it. GraphQL over HTTP tells the client to send application/json;q=0.9. The upstream test client.test.ts line 50 pins the value. Check accept-default.

title: A 400 or 422 reply of application/graphql-response+json gives a NetworkError, not its GraphQL errors
note: src/client.ts line 251 throws NetworkError for each reply that is not ok, before it reads the body. The caller gets "Server responded with 400: Bad Request" and must read error.response again to see the errors. The upstream test "should report invalid request" pins NetworkError on a 400. Check errors-4xx.

title: A media type in a different letter case gives the error Unsupported response content-type
note: src/client.ts lines 256 to 262 compare the content-type with a case-sensitive includes. RFC 9110 makes the type and the subtype case-insensitive. A 200 reply of Application/GraphQL-Response+JSON with data gives the error, not the data. No upstream test pins it. Check media-type-case.

title: The default Accept field gives application/json the same weight as application/graphql-response+json
note: The client sends accept: application/graphql-response+json, application/json when the caller gives no Accept field. GraphQL over HTTP tells the client to send application/json;q=0.9. The caller can set its own Accept field. The upstream test tests/legacy/general.test.ts line 394 pins the value. Check accept-default. Not filed upstream: the default is a deliberate choice of the project, its own test pins it, the rule is a SHOULD, and the caller can set the header.

title: The default Accept field has three more media types, each with the weight of application/graphql-response+json
note: fetchOptions.ts line 153 sends application/graphql-response+json, application/graphql+json, application/json, text/event-stream, multipart/mixed. GraphQL over HTTP tells the client to send application/graphql-response+json, application/json;q=0.9. The caller can set fetchOptions.headers. The upstream test fetchOptions.test.ts line 140 pins the value. Check accept-default. Not filed upstream: the default is a deliberate choice of the project, its own test pins it, the rule is a SHOULD, and the caller can set the header.

title: A 422 reply of a media type in a different letter case gives a ServerError with no GraphQL errors
note: parseAndCheckHttpResponse.ts line 182 compares the content-type with a case-sensitive includes. Thus Application/GraphQL-Response+JSON goes to the JSON path, which throws ServerError for a status of 300 or more. A 200 reply still gives its data. The multipart path of the same file lower-cases the type. No upstream test pins it. Check media-type-case.

title: question.encode returns its input question, not the buffer with the encoded question
note: Each other codec (encode, answer.encode, name.encode and the record codecs) returns the buffer. A caller that encodes one question without a buffer gets the question object back, and the bytes go to a buffer that it never sees.

title: streamDecode ignores the offset that the README documents
note: The README documents streamDecode(buf, [offset]). The function reads the length prefix at byte 0 and decodes from byte 2, so the message at a later offset of a buffer decodes as the first message.

title: streamDecode.bytes does not count the 2-byte length prefix that streamEncode.bytes counts
note: streamDecode.bytes is decode.bytes. A reader of a TCP stream that removes streamDecode.bytes from its buffer after each message is 2 bytes short, and reads the last 2 bytes of the message as the next length prefix. The offset is the same for each message and no peer can choose it, so it is a fault of the API and not a desync that a peer can steer.

title: A real-time socket whose connection ack timed out stays open, and its later close stops the keep-alive check of the new socket
note: After the 15 s ack timeout the provider opens a new socket and does not close the first one. The onclose of the first socket calls _closeSocket on the provider: it clears the keep-alive interval of the new socket and records CLOSED. The Hub reports Disconnected while the new socket delivers data, and a silent new socket is never detected.

title: After a retry that follows a connection ack timeout, the connection state stays ConnectedPendingDisconnect
note: The ack timeout records CONNECTION_FAILED, which sets the intended state to disconnected. The retry does not record OPENING_CONNECTION again, so a working subscription on the retry socket reports ConnectedPendingDisconnect and never Connected.

title: wsLink: an event without an id resets the lastEventId of a subscription, so a reconnect cannot resume after the last tracked event
note: handleResponseMessage sets params.lastEventId to result.id for each data event, also when the id is undefined. After a reconnect the client subscribes again with no lastEventId. httpSubscriptionLink and the SSE server keep the last tracked id (trpc #7691).

title: Pool.query over HTTP (poolQueryViaFetch) sends the source text of a password function as the password
note: The HTTP path of NeonPool.query builds the connection string with encodeURIComponent(password). node-postgres and neon() accept a password function, so the server gets the text of the function and the login fails. A pool with no password sends the text null.

title: @libsql/hrana-client (Hrana 3 protobuf) reads StepEndEntry.last_insert_rowid as uint64, not sint64
note: The fault is in @libsql/hrana-client 0.10.0, the Hrana client of @libsql/client 0.18.0. The Hrana 3 spec and the libsql server encode the field as sint64 (zigzag), as StmtResult.last_insert_rowid. The client reads the zigzag value, so a cursor batch gives 10 for rowid 5. @libsql/client opens Hrana 2 and does not use cursors: the fault needs openWs or openHttp with protocol version 3.
